お金[かね]を 入[い]れたんですが、 切符[きっぷ]が 出[で]ません。
I put money in, but the ticket didn’t come out.
Travel

"お金を入れたんですが" means "I put in the money, but..." The verb "入れる" (ireru) means "to put in," and "お金" (okane) means "money." The "たんですが" at the end adds a nuance of explanation or reason, similar to saying "but..." in English. "切符が出ません" means "the ticket is not coming out." "切符" (kippu) means "ticket," and "出ません" (demasen) is the negative form of the verb "出る" (deru), meaning "to come out" or "to be dispensed."
